candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: follow emergency response plans, protect clients and healthcare personnel from environmental hazards, and use safety procedures appropriately.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — facility emergency action and fire safety
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize core OSHA emergency-action-plan elements, including emergency reporting, evacuation/exit routes, personnel accountability, and assigned rescue or medical duties when applicable.

options.A: Procedures for reporting an emergency, evacuation and exit-route assignments, accounting for personnel, and designated rescue or medical duties when applicable.
options.B: A plan to keep all personnel at their workstations until an external agency arrives, regardless of evacuation instructions or immediate hazards.
options.C: A requirement that only managers know the evacuation route so staff movement can be controlled during an emergency.
options.D: A policy to disable alarms during drills and emergencies so patients are not disturbed by warning signals.

candidate.rationale: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38 requires an emergency action plan to include, at minimum, procedures for reporting fires or other emergencies; emergency evacuation procedures and exit-route assignments; procedures for critical operations before evacuation when applicable; accounting for employees after evacuation; rescue and medical duties for designated employees; and contact information for plan questions. OSHA also requires an employee alarm system and training/review of the plan. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A workplace emergency action plan includes procedures for reporting emergencies, evacuation and exit routes, accounting for personnel, designated rescue/medical duties when applicable, alarm systems, and employee training/review.
candidate.source_locator: 29 CFR 1910.38(c) Minimum elements of an emergency action plan; §1910.38(d) Employee alarm system; §1910.38(e)-(f) training/review requirements.
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Department of Labor, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA)
candidate.stem: Which element is expected in a healthcare facility emergency action plan for fire or another workplace emergency?
